column1: # The receiver each of Phase 5i's introspection rows is sent to in
# corpus/introspection-arity.tsv's probe (Phase 5i Task 0).
# class<TAB>arm<TAB>setup<TAB>wrapper<TAB>directives
# `setup` is statements separated by ` | `, which must leave `r` holding the
# receiver. `directives` is directive text, also ` | `-separated, appended
# after the program; `--` is none.
# `wrapper` is `call`, which puts the setup and the send inside an internal
# routine called from the main program with two arguments, or `--`, which
# leaves both at the top level. THE TWO MECHANISMS EXIST BECAUSE THE PROBE
# WRITES ONE FILE AND RUNS IT: a receiver that needs a ::routine, ::method or
# ::class to exist needs it in the same file, and a receiver that describes a
# caller needs a caller. Measured on the oracle 2026-09-07, both halves:
# `.context~stackFrames` has one entry at the top level and two inside a call,
# and a RexxContext built inside a call is DEAD in the caller -- reading one
# there is `98.981 Target RexxContext is no longer active`. A StackFrame, by
# contrast, survives its own frame's exit and still answers ~name, ~line,
# ~traceLine and ~arguments.
# THE SETUP IS THE RICHEST RECEIVER THE ORACLE CAN BUILD, not the richest both
# sides can. A class whose state this crate does not have fails here rather
# than at the send, and the probe reports that as `setup-differs` -- which is
# the phase's headline measurement and not a harness fault.
# Pointer's and Buffer's INSTANCE arm is absent BY NAME rather than by
# silence, the way collection_scopes.rs excludes RexxQueue.
# corpus/docs/class-set.txt gives them no construction expression -- the
# reference says instances come only from native code (utilityclasses.xml:429,
# :6910) -- so no receiver exists to send to and every instance row of theirs
# would be setup-differs on the oracle's own side. Naming them keeps "a row
# with no receiver is a failure" available as a signal for a class that is
# supposed to have one. Their CLASS arm is here: `.Pointer` needs no
# construction, and `new` is the row Phase 5i owns.
# THE Method RECEIVER IS A REXX METHOD ON PURPOSE. class-set.txt's own is
# `.Object~method('objectName')`, which is native; measured 2026-09-07 its
# ~source is an EMPTY Array where `.K~method('MM')`'s has one line, and the
# seven is* flags are identical on both (only isGuarded is 1), so the native
# receiver cannot discriminate a body that reads the source from one that
# answers an empty Array.
# THE Package RECEIVER IS A PROGRAM'S PACKAGE ON PURPOSE, for the same reason.
# class-set.txt's own is `.Class~package`, the REXX package; measured
# 2026-09-07 that answers name REXX, sourceSize 0, source Array(0), and EMPTY
# tables for routines, publicRoutines, resources, definedMethods and
# namespaces -- only classes (67) and publicClasses (62) have content. Every
# Package row in method-bodies.txt is measured against that.
# The probe directory also holds `source.rex`, a one-line `return 1` written
# by the harness, because the probe writes one file and a row taking a file
# name needs a second one -- naming the running program would re-execute it.
# Measured 2026-09-07, the Package receiver's tables: classes 3,
# publicClasses 2, routines 2, publicRoutines 2, definedMethods 2,
# resources 2. importedPackages is 0 and cannot be made otherwise here: a
# ::requires needs a file on this build's search path and nothing is on it --
# rxregexp.cls, json.cls and socket.cls all answer 43.901 rc 213.
